newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Members of the "Yellow Bird" organisation, which has helped China's pro-democracy activists escape overseas since 1989, will leave Hong Kong before the end of the month for fear of being persecuted after the handover.

-- A Taiwan official said Taiwanese organisation in Hong Kong could not be grouped in one building after the handover due to objections from Beijing. The paper said China felt having all Taiwan organisations under one roof would give them a more "official" colour.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Seven thousand people took to the streets in Hong Kong to urge China to reevaluate the Tiananmen protests of 1989. The organiser, the Hong Kong Alon the handover day "at all costs", even thought it might not get police approval.

-- WEN WEI PO -- U.S. President Bill Clinton announced five diplomatic policies, and maintaining the stability of Asia was among them. He stressed that the world should not isolate China, and Sino-US economic and trade relations should be strengthened.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- China Travel confirmed it acquired 51 percent of Sun Fook Kong and that it would inject several real estate developments in Hong Kong and China into its new unit.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Improving consumer confidence underpinned a 65 percent jump in total vehicle sales in Hong Kong in the first four months of the year, with passenger vehicles showing a 59 percent increase.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Scores of Hong Kong developers, including New World Development and Sun Hung Kai, are bidding for a 2.1 billion yuan infrastructure and property project between Hong Kong and China, the Shenzhen link to the territory's planned Western Corridor Railway.

-- A Chinese foreign trade official said China hoped the change to a Labour government might enhance Sino-British trade ties. He said China hoped to discuss ways of further developing bilateral trade and economic relations with the United Kingdom.
